cf.title: Report userid to PgBackendStatus for standalone backends

input.subject: [PATCH] Report userid to PgBackendStatus for standalone backends

verdict_reasoning: Only demand-1 survived, and it fails level 1b on demand. Message #2 asked who benefits when no other process can read the status of a postgres --single backend, and message #3 answered that the empty user name looks strange but is harmless. The change is small and costs users of normal servers nothing, so this is a "not now, show demand" outcome and no rejection of the idea.

brief.title: Report the user ID in backend status for single-user mode backends
brief.problem: In single-user mode (postgres --single), pg_stat_activity shows no user name for the session. The author found this by querying pg_stat_activity in single-user mode and calls it strange but harmless. The thread names no user who needs the information.
brief.proposed_design: The standalone backend always runs as the bootstrap superuser, and the patch records that user ID in its PgBackendStatus entry. Only src/backend/utils/activity/backend_status.c changes.
user_visible_surface: pg_stat_activity in single-user mode shows usesysid and usename for the session instead of empty values.
author_claims: Standalone backends always use the bootstrap superuser.
Reporting it lets users see the user in pg_stat_activity even in single-user mode.
The current empty user name is strange but harmless.
brief.thread_state: Michael Paquier asked why this matters, since no other process can read the status of a postgres --single backend. The author replied that the empty user name only looks strange; nobody else has replied.
unclear: The proposal does not say whether other columns in pg_stat_activity are also empty or wrong in single-user mode.
The patch has no test and no documentation change.
The proposal does not say whether bootstrap mode (initdb) takes the same code path and is affected.

objections.title: No user is shown to need the user name in single-user mode
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA runs postgres --single to recover from wraparound and queries pg_stat_activity. Only that one session can see its own row, and the DBA already knows it runs as the bootstrap superuser. The patch gives this user nothing new, and a committer still takes on a change to backend status startup.
objections.argument: Message #2 asked why this matters when no other process can read the status of a postgres --single backend. Message #3 does not name a use. It says the empty user name "looks a bit strange though harmless" and that the author noticed it while querying in single-user mode. The thread contains no field report, no request from another user, and no tool that reads usename in single-user mode. The patch is small, but small cost does not replace a stated user problem.
objections.author_must_show: Which tool or recovery procedure reads usesysid or usename from pg_stat_activity in single-user mode, and what goes wrong for it today?

critic.reasoning: Message #2 asked who benefits, and message #3 answered only that the empty user name "looks a bit strange though harmless". The change is small and costs non-users nothing, but the thread names no user, tool or procedure that needs it.

refuted.title: session_user already answers this inside the single-user session
refuted.failure_scenario: An admin in `postgres --single` who wants to know the session's user runs `select session_user` and gets the bootstrap superuser today. The patch only fills usesysid and usename in a pg_stat_activity row that only that same session can read. The project keeps a standalone-only branch in backend_status.c for a cosmetic gap.
refuted.argument: In single-user mode there is one backend, and no other process can read its status entry (message #2). That backend can already get its user from `session_user` or `current_user`, which give the same answer the patch would put in pg_stat_activity. Message #3 says the current state is "harmless" and only "looks a bit strange", so this is about convenience. A committer would likely ask what the patch adds beyond the existing function, small as the change is.
refuted.author_must_show: Which tool or workflow in single-user mode reads pg_stat_activity and cannot use session_user to learn the user?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1. Both rest on message #2 and the "harmless" reply in message #3; the session_user point answers a need the author did not claim, since the proposal is about an empty column looking strange.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The patch adds a case for standalone backends to backend status setup in backend_status.c.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: Only the single-user session can read its own pg_stat_activity row, and the thread names no user who needs usename there.

questions: Which tool or recovery procedure reads usesysid or usename from pg_stat_activity in single-user mode, and what goes wrong for it today?
Does bootstrap mode (initdb) take the same code path, and what does the patch record there?
Are other pg_stat_activity columns also empty or wrong in single-user mode, and why does the patch fill only the user ID?

committability.owner_note: Michael Paquier replied in message #2 and questioned the need; the owner would be someone who knows the backend status and activity reporting code.
committability.liability: One extra case for standalone backends in backend status setup, kept correct if that setup or bootstrap mode changes later. The liability is small and has no on-disk or wire consequence.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered the committer's question within a day in message #3; no sign either way about post-commit fixes.

not_now.evidence_that_would_change_it: A named tool, monitoring query or recovery procedure that reads usesysid or usename from pg_stat_activity in single-user mode and misbehaves on the empty value, or a report from another user who hit this.

priority.reason: The patch changes one file and is 1.1 KiB, so cost is low, but it affects only postgres --single sessions and message #3 calls the current state harmless. It is worth reviewer time once a use is shown.

provisional_note: Without the code, nobody could check whether bootstrap mode (initdb) takes the same path, or at which point in backend status setup the user ID is recorded.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Trigger failsafe when VACUUM is run in single user mode
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a VACUUM option for single-user mode, first called VACUUM LIMIT and later VACUUM (EMERGENCY), that vacuums only tables whose xid or mxid age passes a fixed cutoff, with failsafe behavior and no index cleanup or truncation. The aim is to get out of single-user mode quickly after a wraparound shutdown.
precedents_retrieved.objection: During review, the thread found that the v14 failsafe already turns off heap truncation, so plain VACUUM should work under the postmaster at xidStopLimit. The plan then moved to removing the advice to use single-user mode. Noah Misch then showed that VACUUM can still create multixacts at multiStopLimit, so more work was needed. The author was away sick and withdrew the work for v15.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I gather from subsequent discussion that a full solution goes beyond just a new warning message and documentation. Either way I'm not quite prepared to address this in time for v15.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix Deadlock Issue in Single User Mode When IO Failure Occurs
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a hang in single-user mode when a relation read or write fails during startup recovery or a checkpoint: AbortBufferIO() at process exit waits on a buffer I/O lwlock that the process still holds. It makes sure all lwlocks are released before AbortBufferIO() runs, first by registering LWLockReleaseAll() as an exit callback and in v3 by calling it in AtProcExit_Buffers().
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila tested the create table, insert and checkpoint repro and reported that the patch does not fix the problem. The second I/O error, raised during ShutdownXLOG() at exit, now ends in an assertion failure in UnpinBuffer() called from ReleaseAuxProcessResources. Michael Paquier reproduced the same trace and asked the author for an update, but the author did not respond, so the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I have tried to look into this patch and I don't think it fixes the
problem.

precedents_retrieved.title: System username in pg_stat_activity
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an authname column to pg_stat_activity that shows the externally authenticated user name, the same value the SYSTEM_USER keyword returns. It also covers methods such as peer and ident, which have no view of their own like pg_stat_gss.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread stopped in February 2024 during an open discussion about whether pg_stat_activity already has too many columns and should be split into several views. Magnus Hagander replied that moving columns would break existing monitoring tools, and no one answered. Michael Paquier marked the entry Returned with feedback in October 2024 because nobody had posted since.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This is the last message sent on this thread, and an entry was still registered in the CF app, so I am marking that as RwF for now.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_stat_activity: avoid showing state=active with wait_event=ClientRead
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_stat_activity read each backend's state and wait event in one pass, so active backends no longer show wait_event ClientRead under high load. It also changes how the local copy of backend status is allocated, using chunks instead of one allocation sized by max_connections.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas argued that the state and the wait event are set by different functions at different times, so any reader can see them out of step and the patch can only narrow the race. He said these lightweight introspection views were never meant to be consistent with each other, and that making them so would add complexity and slow the system down. The thread ends with the authors asking for the patch plus a documentation note, and no reply is shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The very best a patch like this can hope to do is narrow the
race condition enough that the discrepancies are observed less
frequently in practice.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add single-item cache when looking at topmost XID of a subtrans XID"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add single-item cache when looking at topmost XID of a subtrans XID"
Reverted commit(s): Add single-item cache when looking at topmost XID of a subtrans XID
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 06f5295 as per issues with this approach, both in
terms of efficiency impact and stability.  First, contrary to the
single-item cache for transaction IDs in transam.c, the cache may finish
by not be hit for a long time, and without an invalidation mechanism to
clear it, it would cause inconsistent results on wraparound for
example.  Second, the use of SubTransGetTopmostTransaction() for the
caching has a limited impact on performance.  SubTransGetParent() could
have more impact, though the benchmarking of the single-item approach
still needs to be proved, particularly under the conditions where SLRU
lookups are stressed in parallel with overflowed snapshots (aka more
than 64 subxids generated, for example).

After discussion with Andres Freund.

precedents_retrieved.title: Display individual query in pg_stat_activity
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the query column of pg_stat_activity to show only the statement that is running when a client sends several statements in one simple-protocol query string. It also makes parallel workers started from a function show their individual statement instead of the whole function body.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying and failed the cfbot, and Georgios Kokolatos returned it with feedback on 2020-12-01 after it stayed in Waiting on Author with no new version. Earlier, Dave Page objected that showing only part of the query string makes it harder to match activity to the application or server logs, and suggested a separate field instead. The visible messages do not show this objection being settled.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This patch fails in the cfbot for quite some time now.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prevent incorrect entries in pg_stat_activity.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch stops pg_stat_activity from showing an idle backend with an old xact_start, which happens when ProcessCatchupInterrupt(), RemoveTempRelationsCallback() or Describe message handling run a short transaction without changing the state. The first version reset the statement start timestamp and reported the Describe paths as active; the second hides xact_start and query_start for idle client backends when the view is read.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected to the first version because it adds pgstat_report_activity() calls on common paths and resets the timestamp on every ProcessClientReadInterrupt() call. Tomas Vondra questioned the second version because it hides the bad values when the view is read, and suggested resetting the timestamp where it is set, for example in CommitTransactionCommand(). The visible thread ends with that review in December 2024, with no reply from the author before the entry was closed in October 2025.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It seems a bit strange to "fix" this while querying the data, which I think is what the patch is doing. Wouldn't it be better to make sure we don't have such "incorrect" data in the first place?

precedents_retrieved.title: Addition of authenticated ID to pg_stat_activity
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the authenticated identity, already logged by log_connections, to pg_stat_activity, with a new GUC that sets how much shared memory each backend reserves for it. After concerns about the width of pg_stat_activity, a later version moved authenticated_id and the client_* columns into a new pg_stat_connection view.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch. The thread had been idle for two months with little interest, and moving client_addr, client_hostname and client_port into a new view looked hard to justify for this feature. A reviewer also questioned the server-start GUC for truncating the value and the view's output for internal processes and Unix sockets.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This also includes a split of pg_stat_activity for client_addr, client_hostname and client_port into a new catalog, which may be hard to justify for this feature.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow single table VACUUM in transaction block
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Greg Stark, Robert Haas, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch let VACUUM on a single table run inside a transaction block, so scripts run with --single-transaction would not fail; it skipped PROC_IN_VACUUM and the datfrozenxid update in that case. Later versions forced VACUUM FULL for temp tables and queued an autovacuum request for other tables, and finally added an explicit VACUUM (BACKGROUND) option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers objected to a VACUUM command that runs in-process in some cases and as a background autovacuum request in others. Robert Haas and Tom Lane also rejected making background vacuum the default or controlling it with a GUC, because users would notice the delay and regression tests expect VACUUM to finish at once. The author agreed, switched to an explicit VACUUM (BACKGROUND) option, and proposed returning this entry and opening a new one for that design.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Basically, I am not buying Simon's requirement that this be transparent.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert changes for SSL compression in libpq
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert changes for SSL compression in libpq
Reverted commit(s): Switch back sslcompression to be a normal input field in libpq; Add support for more progress reporting in COPY
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This partially reverts 096bbf7 and 9d2d457, undoing the libpq changes as
it could cause breakages in distributions that share one single libpq
version across multiple major versions of Postgres for extensions and
applications linking to that.

Note that the backend is unchanged here, and it still disables SSL
compression while simplifying the underlying catalogs that tracked if
compression was enabled or not for a SSL connection.

Per discussion with Tom Lane and Daniel Gustafsson.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the corpus returned no earlier attempt at this idea, and no thread message points to an earlier discussion. Desirability, raised by Michael Paquier in message #2, belongs to another angle.

The patch adds no syntax, GUC, catalog entry or dumped object, so pg_dump and psql are unaffected. The only visible change fills usesysid and usename in pg_stat_activity during single-user mode, and no plausible script depends on those columns staying empty. Not checked without the code: whether bootstrap mode (initdb) takes the same path.

The patch changes only in-memory backend status (PgBackendStatus in shared memory) for a standalone backend. It touches no on-disk format, WAL, catalog, wire protocol or replication state, and no other process reads this entry, so this angle has nothing to object to.

No privilege or exposure aspect. A single-user backend runs as the bootstrap superuser with no other sessions, so recording that user ID in its own status entry shows nothing to anyone who could not already see it.

From the maintenance angle there is nothing worth sending. The patch changes one file and only fills a field once for a standalone backend, so users of normal multi-user servers pay no hot-path cost and later features need no new touch point. The weak case for the change belongs to the desirability angle, which Michael Paquier raised in message #2. Without the code I could not check whether bootstrap mode (initdb) takes the same path.
One objection only. The change is small and its cost is low, so the objection is about desirability and is not fatal.
One demand objection only. The cost looks small, so the honest outcome is "not now, show demand" rather than rejection.
